preamble: In this centenary celebration of "26 12" some solutions are not fully defined.

clue.text: Bum on the up, after house in Bath

indicators.note: after places the bottom piece behind the house abbreviation
in a down entry, going up means the word bum's synonym is written bottom to top

parts.note: a bum is a butt, the backside

explanation.surface: Someone's backside rises as they step into the bath after getting home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a large heated bath, often outdoors, that people soak in together.

clue.text: Somewhat like ex-PM that's kind of shady?

parts.note: Gordon Brown was UK prime minister from 2007 to 2010
the suffix -ish means somewhat or rather like

explanation.surface: A jibe that someone resembles a former prime minister, hinting he is a bit dodgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownish describes a tint or shade near brown, so it is a kind of shade or colour; the question mark marks the pun on shady.

clue.text: City team has the last word

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a football or cricket team
amen is said at the end of a prayer, so it is the last word

explanation.surface: A city's sports team gets the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: Xiamen is a port city in Fujian province in south-east China.

clue.text: 10 in pie doled out with stew

indicators.note: doled out means shared out, so the letters of pie and stew are dealt round into a new order

explanation.surface: Birds baked in a pie are served up alongside a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is the cross-reference to 10-across, the word birds, and stands as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peewits are lapwings, plovers named for their call, so they are birds.

clue.text: District with church and city hospital

parts.note: Paris is the French capital city
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An area with a church, a city and a hospital, like a description of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is a local district that has its own church and priest.

clue.text: Indulge Asian creature reportedly extremely 2

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the animal's name stands for a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the giant panda is a bear from China

indicators.note: extremely asks for only the outermost letters of the written-out number

parts.note: the figure 2 is written out as the word two

explanation.surface: Spoil an Asian animal to an extreme degree, by a second-hand account.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent panda and pander sound alike. The 2 looks like a cross-reference to 2-down, but it is just the number, spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pander to someone is to gratify or indulge their wishes.

clue.text: Producer of 24 when the Guardian's in difficulties

indicators.note: in puts the newspaper's possessive inside the word for difficulties

parts.note: fixes are tight spots or difficulties
the puzzle appears in the Guardian, so from the paper's own viewpoint its property is ours

explanation.surface: Something that yields 24 when the newspaper is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Four sixes multiply to 24, so the definition is a sum, not a clock or a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: Four times six makes twenty-four, so four sixes multiplied produce that number.

clue.text: Precocious young girl, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading the word forwards or backwards gives the same letters, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A pert little girl, however you regard her.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a dated term for a pert, precocious or presumptuous girl.

clue.text: Having short dip, first of blue tits saw worm wriggling in novel way

indicators.note: wriggling, moving in a new way, says the gathered letters are rearranged
short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

indicators.note: first of takes just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Bathing briefly, a blue tit first sees a worm writhing.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of DI (dip, short), B, TITS, SAW and WORM. At Swim-Two-Birds (1939) is Flann O'Brien's first novel, defined only by the preamble's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The preamble's theme is Flann O'Brien, and At Swim-Two-Birds is his celebrated first novel.

clue.text: See 9
One lewdly desiring some bicycle chains

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone with lustful longings for a few bike chains, an absurd fetish.
explanation.definitionFit: A lech is a lecher, someone given to lewd sexual desire.

clue.text: See 26
Sort out crime (hot hint: pedal into work)

indicators.note: sort out means put in order, so the letters of the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on tackling crime: pedal your way to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is crime, hot, hint and pedal; the theme novel, The Third Policeman, features policemen obsessed with bicycles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Third Policeman is a novel by Flann O'Brien, so a literary work.

clue.text: See 25
Nearly broken, holding the same sort of memory

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters wrap round the abbreviation for ditto
broken says the letters of nearly are smashed into a new order

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: Something almost broken that keeps the same kind of memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters split so that the abbreviation for ditto sits in the middle of them, which the container shows only by its result.
explanation.definitionFit: Read-only memory, ROM, is computer storage whose contents can be read but not changed.

clue.text: Cover story 5 raised

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in a down entry the pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A cover story is told five times higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LIEV, written in clue order, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a piece of fabric that covers the face or head, so it is a cover.

clue.text: Contents of spoon and cup each put in "flathk" in "a bad story about the 20"

annotationWithheld.why: Clue sound: POO (contents of spoon) and U (contents of cup) go separately into THERMOTH (lisped 'flathk' = Thermos), giving THE(POO)RMO(U)TH; the grammar refuses both a scattered insertion and the needed nested container, so the parse cannot be written.
annotationWithheld.clue: Contents of spoon and cup each put in "flathk" in "a bad story about the 20"

clue.text: Old 27 having surrealist briefly replace second English cyclist?

indicators.note: replace says the shortened name goes in where the second English letter was

parts.note: 27 is policeman; peeler is old slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the last letter of the painter's name

parts.note: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter

explanation.surface: An old officer whose surrealist friend briefly stands in for a second English bike rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second English' names the second E of PEELER; DAL replaces it. The question mark says cyclist is a description, not a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedaller works the pedals of a bicycle, so is a cyclist of sorts.

clue.text: Crazy Horse converted to film again

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the jumbled horse and the word to are rearranged together
crazy means wild, so the letters of horse are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The Sioux chief Crazy Horse is turned into a movie a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy Horse' reads as the Lakota leader's name, but Crazy jumbles horse and 'converted' then reworks it together with to.
explanation.definitionFit: To reshoot a scene is to film it again.

clue.text: Riley endlessly had fun, initially having suffered just the opposite?

indicators.note: having suffered suggests damage, so the gathered letters are knocked into a new order
endlessly means the last letter of the name Riley is removed
initially takes only the opening letter of the word fun

explanation.surface: Riley had fun after a hard time, the reverse of his famous easy life.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'life of Riley' is an idiom for an easy, carefree existence, so its opposite is a hard one; The Hard Life is also a Flann O'Brien novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of the proverbial easy, luxurious life of Riley is a tough, difficult existence.

clue.text: Indulgently affectionate element in man's best friend

indicators.note: in puts the metal inside the animal

parts.note: the dog is proverbially man's best friend
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Some element of fondness inside a pet dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means showing excessive, uncritical fondness, lavishing love on someone.

clue.text: Washing facilities bedsit surprisingly offers

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly, so the letters of the word appear in an unforeseen order

explanation.surface: A small rented flat unexpectedly comes with washing facilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidets are low basins used for washing the lower body.

clue.text: Off day? That is criminal

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
i.e. is short for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone having a bad day turns out to be a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A baddie is a villain or wrongdoer, so a criminal.

clue.text: Great love reformed despicable chap

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are given a new shape

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A great love who has changed his ways, though he was a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: TOERAG is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is British slang for a worthless, contemptible man, a rotter.

clue.text: See 17
Tip-off: bike part involved in thievery (hack's rewritten book)

indicators.note: rewritten means written again in a different order, so all the gathered letters are rearranged
tip off means the tip, the first letter, is taken off

parts.note: a pedal is part of a bicycle
taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A tip-off about a stolen bike part, and a journalist's rewrite of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is EDAL (pedal without P), THIEVERY and HACK. The Dalkey Archive is O'Brien's 1964 novel, set in Dalkey near Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalkey Archive is a novel by Flann O'Brien, so a book.

clue.text: Said tart to old boy: "Nowt French for an Irishman"

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the pastry word stands for the identical-sounding name

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
nowt is northern English for nothing, which in French is rien

explanation.surface: A tart remark to a former pupil, calling him a nobody in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Flann O'Brien was the Irish writer Brian O'Nolan, whose centenary the puzzle marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Flann O'Brien, pen name of Brian O'Nolan, was an Irish novelist and columnist.
